To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we found no SOD-1 mutations among a group of Italian patients with ALS, including individuals with familial and sporadic forms of the disease.
the SOD1 gene was sequenced in 30 patients and 30 controls and no mutations were found.

1) we have not found mutations in 30 Italian patients with ALS (familiali ALS, uncertain familial ALS, sporadic ALS); 2) the distribution of SOD-1 ALS appears to be heterogeneous; 3) the SOD-1 mutation detection rate in our population is lower than that in the North American population.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of a large group of patients with ALS in an attempt to identify the genetic cause of this disorder.
the genetic epidemiology of ALS and with the possible role of SOD-1 mutations in ALS.
the genetic basis of ALS and its possible relationship with other neurodegenerative disorders, such as Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease and Huntington's disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SOD-1 mutations account for 20% of FALS and 2.4% of SALS.
the prevalence of SOD-1 mutation in the general population of ALS patients is 1-2% and that the SOD-1 mutations account for 10-15% of FALS and 5-10% of UFALS.
the SOD-1 mutation is not a common cause of ALS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SOD-1 mutations are rare in Italy.
the absence of SOD-1 mutations in a group of patients with ALS does not exclude the possibility of a SOD-1 mutation in other patients with ALS.
SOD-1 mutations account for a very low percentage of ALS patients in Italy, and that the SOD-1 mutation detection should be restricted to patients with FALS and, possibly, to those with SALS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the absence of a mutation in the SOD-1 genes does not exclude the diagnosis of FALS.
the absence of a mutation in a single individual with a familial or sporadic form of ALS does not exclude a possible SOD-1 mutation in the patient's relatives.
SOD-1 mutations should be considered as a rare cause of FALS and UFALS in the Italian population.
